<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Along one actual history, unfinished current-rule steps that lower a remaining certificate, together with a non-increasing handoff at the actual reached stage, feed the existing finite-renewal theorem and ensure completion within its bound. Explicit correspondence to actual new generation supplies the premise of the existing positive-ground theorem of living significance; the realized form may change. Individually finishing rules and local progress at every step do not alone guarantee realization under repeated revision. The result is stated on the shared Frame/Run, and the exact instance of the inherited living-significance condition is checked using relevance read from significance; the finite-realization and failure scopes are unchanged.

Canonical source: [Handoff.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Handoff.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Actual indexed histories, steps, natural-number certificates, decidable completion events and an initial bound are supplied; unfinished local descent and non-increasing handoff at the same reached stage are separate hypotheses.
- Completion corresponds to actual newly formed generative content in the same history, with different content allowed across histories. The historical generic form takes explicit G0; P89 derives its instance from Unrestricted, whose significance condition is not derived from progress.
- Transport from admitted scope to actuality requires actual coverage and execution/support correspondence. Permission, real losses and still-valid specific undertakings require judgment under existing practical principles.

Stages, organizational rules and revisions differentiate within shared activity, without a primitive external controller or private value owners. Certificates support a specified finite realization bound; if event n denotes transition n to n+1, events 0..B comprise at most B+1 transitions. Terminal states named formed do not themselves certify actual goodness or fulfillment.
